mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 3% over the next 60 days reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the subsequent 20-day horizon.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises continuously for 60 days above 3%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during a similar 60-day pre-rising period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a labor market strengthening that boosts investor confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >2% in a month while UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns show no statistically significant correlation with the combined signal (Pearson IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1,500K for three consecutive months indicates accelerating domestic demand, which is associated with higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite HOUST monthly increases above 1,500K for the past 3 months (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 2% for two consecutive months suggests weakening supply-side constraints, which can reduce production costs and support higher equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative and INDPRO remains below its 50-day moving average during the period.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 4% for two consecutive months, the market anticipates a near-term rate hike, which compresses discount rates and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises for two consecutive months above 4%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) despite the inflation signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden one-standard-deviation increase in weekly job openings (PAYEMS) without a corresponding rise in unemployment suggests a tight labor market that can drive risk-on sentiment and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by more than one standard deviation from its 30-day moving average in a single week
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are flat or negative despite the job openings signal.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (not directly observable in the provided proxies; this sketch is invalid under the given observable catalog) cannot be used. Instead, a valid demand signal via supply: A 3-month cumulative decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of over 5% indicates excess demand relative to supply capacity, which can support higher equity valuations and positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO cumulative decline over 3 months exceeds 5%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns show no significant correlation with the cumulative INDPRO decline (Pearson IC > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising), S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days tend to be negative due to higher discount rates applied to future cash flows, regardless of other macro variables.
candidate_trigger: any regime where FEDFUNDS is rising
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (t-test p < 0.01) during a FEDFUNDS rising period.
